scenario: AITA For going on my best friend's dream trip and not inviting her? | Me and Mandy have been best friends since basically kindergarten, and almost since then she's been fascinated with Turkey, Croatia, and the Balkans/Mediterranean region in general. I started dating a guy from a Balkan country and was making plans to go visit him and his family, and while doing so I found this AMAZING package deal that lets you travel the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey and Morocco. Seriously, it was like a once in a lifetime deal and though it's pretty expensive, it's WAY cheaper than it would be to find places to stay and travel to those places on your own. I KNEW Mandy couldn't afford it, and I KNEW it would hurt her deeply that she wasn't getting a chance to go. This trip is literally what she dreams of doing, and with me in particular, but she's been in a lot of financial trouble lately. So I told her I was planning a trip, but not any of the details. I also told another very close friend about the trip, and she looked up the same deal and decided she wanted to go as well. I said I'd love to have the company, so she bought her tickets and she's coming along too. I realized that if Mandy heard about this or found out about this before I got a chance to tell her she'd be super hurt, so I told her about the trip. She was SOOOOOOO upset. She asked about why I didn't invite her, and I told her it was because I knew she couldn't afford it and I thought it would just be salt in the wound. (I also privately think she would have made some very questionable decisions in order to fund the trip, or would have gone and then not had enough for money, or her bills, or things like that at home.) That just made it worse, and she cried, and cried about how we always said we'd go and experience those places together, and that I don't even have any interest in the region, which is pretty much true since I want to travel around Asia. I told her we could still go that in the future, and we could even do this trip in the future, but she was too hurt to want to hear that. My boyfriend thinks I am being kind of a dick, and says for his best friend, he'd have offered to pay for part to help if he could, and I guess I \*could\* but not super comfortably and idk when she'd pay me back. He also thinks she'd have been less hurt if I brought it up while I was thinking about it. My other friend agrees that it was a good idea to wait to tell her since she agrees Mandy probably would have done ANYTHING to go on that trip.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to go on this trip without inviting my best friend Mandy. Let me start by laying out the situation as I understand it. Mandy and I have been best friends since kindergarten. She's always been fascinated with Turkey, Croatia, and the Balkans. I started dating someone from a Balkan country and made plans to visit him and his family. While doing that, I found this amazing travel package that covers the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey, and Morocco. It's a once-in-a-lifetime deal, but it's pretty expensive. However, it's way cheaper than finding places to stay and travel on my own. I know Mandy can't afford it, and I know it would hurt her deeply that she's not getting the chance to go. This trip is literally what she's always dreamed of doing, especially with me. But she's been in a lot of financial trouble lately. So I told her I was planning a trip but didn't give any details. I also told another very close friend about the trip, and she looked up the same deal and decided she wanted to go too. I said I'd love to have her company, so she bought her tickets and is coming along. I realized that if Mandy heard about this or found out before I got a chance to tell her, she'd be super hurt. So I told her about the trip. She was so upset. She asked why I didn't invite her, and I told her it was because I knew she couldn't afford it and I thought it would just be salt in the wound. I also privately think she would have made some very questionable decisions in order to fund the trip or would have gone and then not have enough money for bills or things at home. That just made it worse, and she cried and cried about how we always said we'd go and experience those places together. She also said I don't even have any interest in the region, which is pretty much true since I want to travel around Asia. I told her we could still go in the future and could even do this trip in the future, but she was too hurt to want to hear that. My boyfriend thinks I'm being kind of a dick and says that for his best friend, he'd have offered to pay for part of it if he could, and I guess I could but not super comfortably and I don't know when she'd pay me back. He also thinks she'd have been less hurt if I brought it up while I was thinking about it. My other friend agrees that it was a good idea to wait to tell her since she agrees Mandy probably would have done anything to go on that trip. So, is it right or wrong for me to go on this trip without inviting Mandy? Let me think through this step by step. First, I need to consider the friendship. Mandy and I have been friends for a long time, and this trip is something she's always wanted to do with me. By not inviting her, I'm potentially breaking a promise we made to each other. That's a big deal because trust is a crucial part of any friendship. Next, I have to think about the reasons I didn't invite her. I knew she couldn't afford it, and I was worried it would hurt her. I also thought she might make poor financial decisions to go, which could cause more problems for her. But by not inviting her, I'm causing her emotional pain, which might be worse than the financial stress she could have faced. I also need to consider how I handled the situation. I told her about the trip after she found out through another friend, which made her even more upset. If I had brought it up earlier, maybe she wouldn't have been as hurt. My boyfriend suggested offering to help with the costs, which is a kind gesture, but I'm not comfortable doing that financially. Another point is that I have another friend going with me, which might make Mandy feel excluded. She might feel like she's not as important as my other friend, which could strain our friendship further. I also have to think about my own feelings and needs. I want to travel around Asia, not the Balkans, so this trip isn't something I'm as passionate about. But Mandy is, so it's important to her. By not including her, I'm prioritizing my own plans over her desires, which might not be fair. On the other hand, I'm considering the practical aspects. The trip is expensive, and I can't afford to help her out financially. I also don't want to put her in a position where she has to take on more debt or make poor financial decisions. But by not inviting her, I'm causing emotional harm, which might be harder to repair. I also need to think about how to make things right. Maybe I can plan a future trip where we can both go, but Mandy is too hurt right now to consider that. My boyfriend's suggestion to offer help financially is a good one, but I'm not sure if I can do that. Maybe I can find a way to contribute a little, even if it's not the full amount. In the end, I have to weigh the emotional impact on Mandy against the practical reasons for not inviting her. It seems like not inviting her caused significant hurt, which might have been avoided if I had handled the situation differently, like talking to her earlier or offering some financial help. So, considering all these factors, I think it's wrong to go on the trip without inviting Mandy. The emotional harm and broken trust might outweigh the practical reasons, especially since there could have been ways to include her or handle the situation more sensitively.
